solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Waved sword I discarded

parts.note: a brand is an old literary word for a sword
taken as written
to shed is to cast off or discard

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their weapon after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a weapon is to wave or flourish it, so the past tense matches waved.

clue.text: Polish fan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shine or rub up a surface
second meaning: an enthusiast for something

explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests someone from Poland; it is just the verb polish at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rubbing to a shine and a noun for an enthusiast, as in film buff.

clue.text: Someone else hiding ring in part of flower

indicators.note: the outer word hides the other letter by enclosing it

parts.note: the anther is the pollen-bearing part of a stamen
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A different person conceals a ring in a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more or a different person, as in 'ask another'.

clue.text: Set apart bizarre thing I'd issued

indicators.note: something bizarre is twisted out of the ordinary, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these words are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside a strange item they handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be distinguished from others is to be marked out as different, separated.

clue.text: Asian food doctor found in another continent repeatedly

indicators.note: the doctor is located inside the other letters

parts.note: SA abbreviates South America, written twice
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A physician discovers Asian cooking on a different continent again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian' is part of the definition, so the continent is not Asia but South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry with a spiced filling, from South Asian cuisine.

clue.text: Surpassed speed in East End, oddly

indicators.note: the speed word sits inside the selected letters
oddly keeps the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the phrase East End

parts.note: the phrase whose odd-numbered letters are kept, the district of east London
clip means pace, as in 'at a fair clip'

explanation.surface: Someone drove fast in London's East End and was outdone.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the working-class district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to outshine it, so eclipsed matches surpassed.

clue.text: A variable fashion feature that may be said to attract attention

definitions.text: that may be said to attract attention

parts.note: taken as written
a hem is part of a garment, and hemlines rise and fall with fashion

explanation.surface: A changeable detail of clothing that catches the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahem' is the little cough a person utters to get noticed, hence 'said'.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a polite throat-clearing noise spoken to make others notice you.

clue.text: Star no longer consumes a little coffee, we hear

parts.note: to have something is to eat or drink it

indicators.note: we hear tells you to go by how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a bean is a small unit of coffee

explanation.surface: A faded celebrity drinks a small espresso.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose fame or success is in the past, a former celebrity.

clue.text: Wanting to control cash flow, painter is absorbed in his work

parts.note: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so the small word goes within the other

parts.note: the painter's work is art
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist engrossed in painting wants to manage money flow.
explanation.walkthrough: Monetarism is the economic doctrine that controlling money supply controls inflation.
explanation.definitionFit: A monetarist policy aims to regulate the money supply circulating in an economy.

clue.text: Salvageable stuff fellow almost abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild or unrestrained, so these letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man nearly left behind something worth recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like it trims a word, but it is simply anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is wreckage or cargo found floating after a shipwreck, which may be recovered.

clue.text: Actress initially is embraced by male with pride in affair

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so the inner letters go within the outer word

parts.note: a lion is the male of a pride of big cats

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Actress

parts.note: only its first letter is taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actress is caught up in a romance with a proud man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' is the collective noun for lions, not vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a romantic or sexual relationship, often a secret one, so an affair.

clue.text: They work in theatres to prepare for cuts being made

definitions.meaning: suggests stage actors, but these are operating theatres in hospitals

definitions.text: to prepare for cuts being made
definitions.meaning: suggests editing a script, but the cuts are surgical incisions

explanation.walkthrough: Theatres and cuts both read as drama terms; in a hospital they are the operating room and the surgeon's incision.
explanation.definitionFit: These doctors put patients under before surgery so the surgeon can operate painlessly.

clue.text: Somehow retain, perhaps, people sure to succeed

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unstated way, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be shuffled

explanation.surface: Successors to a throne might somehow keep their place.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs apparent are those whose inheritance cannot be displaced, so they will certainly take over.

clue.text: Redraft was altered later

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: these words provide the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rewrite was changed at a later stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards is an adverb meaning subsequently, at a later time.

clue.text: Hunt lasting very long time

parts.note: 'for' expresses duration, as in lasting for an hour
an age is informally a very long stretch of time

explanation.surface: A chase that goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search or rummage around for food or supplies.

clue.text: Some areas one reconnoitres as rational type

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run spanning them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of areas, all of one and the start of reconnoitres

explanation.surface: A scout surveys certain territories with a logical mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoner is someone who thinks logically, a sensible and rational sort of person.

clue.text: First part of plant consumed by land turtle

indicators.note: being consumed by something puts you inside it

parts.note: terrain is a stretch of land

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word plant

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A tortoise eats the first shoots of a plant on dry ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like part of the definition, as in a land turtle, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, kept as a pet in many homes.

clue.text: Contemplate large vessel for cosmetic

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it thoughtfully
a liner is a big passenger ship

explanation.surface: Gazing at a big ship and thinking of makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is a makeup product drawn along the eyelids.

clue.text: Woman originally holding a signal for person rescued

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Eve was the original woman in Genesis
taken as written
a cue is a signal to begin

explanation.surface: A woman first gives a signal to save someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like a first-letter indicator, but it points to the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An evacuee is someone moved out of danger, as children were from British cities in the war.

clue.text: So-called father that divides capital

definitions.meaning: the river is personified as 'Old Father' in English tradition
the river runs through London, splitting it into north and south

explanation.surface: Reads like a patriarch who splits an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames is London's river, traditionally called Old Father Thames; 'capital' is the city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: London's principal waterway flows through the city centre, separating its northern and southern halves.

clue.text: A German guy rises to the top as executive

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising moves the man from the end up to the start

parts.note: guy is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German fellow climbs to become a top executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager runs a business or department, an executive role.

clue.text: Give bad marks to, various grades one repeated

parts.note: D, E, F, A and C are all exam or school grades
one of those grades, E, appears a second time

explanation.surface: A teacher marks harshly, giving several grades, one twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad marks' looks like poor grades, but it means damage scrawled on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface something is to spoil its surface with graffiti or scratches.

clue.text: Showing effects of exposure, bananas are wet beneath

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: these three words supply all the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fruit left out underneath the rain shows wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weather-beaten is worn or tanned by long exposure to wind, sun and rain.

clue.text: Singer having run in one club, say

indicators.note: the run letter goes inside the bid

parts.note: in bridge, one club is a bid
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A vocalist runs into a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a venue; it is the bridge suit, and 'one club' is a call in the auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Songbirds sing, so a bird is a singer in crossword-speak.

clue.text: Group together make a score of nineteen, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to gather people or animals into one place

definitions.text: make a score of nineteen, for example
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to raise a number to the next whole figure, as nineteen becomes twenty, a score

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like points in a game, but it is the old word for twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both collecting cattle or suspects together and increasing a figure to a neater value.

clue.text: Weapon, for instance, used in inconclusive attack

indicators.note: the example is put to use inside the other word, placed within it
without its conclusion, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to assail is to attack
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An example of an arm deployed in an assault that peters out.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples.

clue.text: Supreme deity put back in place in Egypt

indicators.note: put back reads as turned backwards, so the god's name runs the other way

parts.note: Zeus was the king of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A top god is returned to a spot in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is an Egyptian port city at the southern end of the famous canal.

clue.text: No crudeness cut, when edited — like this

definitions.text: No crudeness cut, when edited — like this

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: taken as written, before the trim

explanation.surface: A censor's note that nothing coarse was removed during editing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: something with no crudeness cut out is unexpurgated.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncensored material has had nothing removed or suppressed by an official censor.
